description: List a webhook endpoint's delivery log, newest first: every delivery to it from the last 30 days, with how the receiver answered. Use it to find out why an event did or didn't arrive. Each row has eventId (evt_…, the webhook-id header the receiver got), eventType, resourceId (the post id for post events, the account id for account events, the endpoint id for webhook.test, null for a sample), status, attempts (each with n, at, statusCode, latencyMs and error), lastStatusCode, lastErrorCode, nextAttemptAt, completedAt and payload (the body exactly as sent). status is SUCCEEDED, FAILED (every attempt failed, the receiver answered 410 Gone, or the event was too large to send), PENDING (still being delivered: a nextAttemptAt in the future means a retry is scheduled, up to 8 attempts over about a day) or SKIPPED (not sent because the endpoint was off when the delivery came due, possibly after failed attempts; while an endpoint is off, its PENDING rows end this way unless it is turned back on before they come due). Error codes: timeout, connection, tls, redirect (redirects are not followed), http_4xx, http_5xx, gone (410), blocked_address (PostFast refused to connect because the hostname resolved to a private address), exhausted, payload_too_large (the event was too large to send) and internal (PostFast's own failure, not the receiver's). Only the receiver's status code is kept, never its response body. totalCount and pageInfo.hasNextPage are filled only when getCount is true, so ask for it on the first page; without it, a full page may have more after it. An id that isn't in this workspace, or was deleted, gives an empty page rather than an error; get_webhook_endpoint tells whether it exists.

getCount.description: Count the whole log, which fills totalCount and pageInfo.hasNextPage. Ask for it on the first page only.

limit.description: Deliveries per page (max 100; every row carries the full event payload)

name: list_webhook_deliveries
title: List Webhook Deliveries
